_comment: Seed data for Rellio Sacred Map. Adherent estimates are approximate (early 2020s). Colors are tuned to the cosmic/space art direction in the current Sacred Map mockup; each is visually distinct on a dark background.

religions.name: Islam
religions.summary: A monotheistic faith founded on revelations received by the Prophet Muhammad in Mecca and Medina, centered on submission to the one God (Allah). Its sacred geography runs from Mecca and Medina across the early Islamic world.

religions.name: Christianity
religions.summary: A monotheistic faith centered on the life, teachings, death, and (in Christian belief) resurrection of Jesus of Nazareth. It spread from Jerusalem and Galilee across the Roman world and beyond.

religions.name: Judaism
religions.origin_region: Ancient Near East / Land of Israel
religions.founding_period: Roots in the 2nd millennium BCE; formalized over many centuries
religions.summary: One of the oldest monotheistic traditions, built on the covenant between God and the people of Israel. Its sacred geography centers on Jerusalem and the wider Land of Israel.

religions.name: Hinduism
religions.founding_period: No single founder; Vedic roots from c. 1500 BCE, often called Sanatana Dharma (ancient/eternal tradition)
religions.primary_text: Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, epics (Ramayana, Mahabharata)
religions.summary: A family of ancient Indian traditions without a single founder, spanning many deities, philosophies, and practices. Its sacred geography is woven across India's rivers, mountains, and temple cities.

religions.name: Sikhism
religions.summary: A monotheistic faith founded by Guru Nanak and shaped by ten successive Gurus, emphasizing devotion to one God, equality, and service. Its sacred geography is concentrated in Punjab.

religions.name: Buddhism
religions.origin_region: Northern Indian subcontinent (Ganges plain and Himalayan foothills)
religions.founding_period: c. 5th century BCE (Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha)
religions.primary_text: Tripitaka (Pali Canon) and many later sutras
religions.summary: A tradition founded on the awakening of Siddhartha Gautama and his teaching of a path to liberation from suffering. It spread from the Ganges plain across Asia and the world.

religions.name: Shintoism
religions.adherents_estimate: Difficult to quantify; widely practiced across Japan, often alongside Buddhism
religions.founding_period: Indigenous to Japan; ancient/prehistoric origins, formalized as a distinct tradition over later centuries
religions.primary_text: Kojiki and Nihon Shoki (early chronicles); no single scripture
religions.summary: Japan's indigenous tradition, centered on kami (spirits/deities) present in nature and ancestors. It is defined less by founding events and more by continuous ritual and sacred places (shrines, mountains).
